item.text:
**1B.3 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Bottom line: I found solid 2024 evidence that Thailand, under Srettha’s government, was engaged in nuclear-security and radiation-safety strengthening. The best evidence is institutional rather than personal: an IAEA mission found a robust framework but also pointed to specific improvements still needed. I did not find direct evidence of any custody failure, accident, or command-and-control breakdown tied to Srettha in 2024.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [IAEA Mission to Thailand Finds a Robust Framework for Nuclear Security Arrangements, Encourages Improvements](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/iaea-mission-to-thailand-finds-a-robust-framework-for-nuclear-security-arrangements-encourages-improvements) | International Atomic Energy Agency | September 13, 2024 | https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/iaea-mission-to-thailand-finds-a-robust-framework-for-nuclear-security-arrangements-encourages-improvements | Strong positive evidence for 1B.3. The IAEA said Thailand had established a robust framework to manage material out of regulatory control, and noted that detection-and-response arrangements were well addressed within Thailand’s legal framework. | `1B.3` |
| [IAEA Mission to Thailand Finds a Robust Framework for Nuclear Security Arrangements, Encourages Improvements](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/iaea-mission-to-thailand-finds-a-robust-framework-for-nuclear-security-arrangements-encourages-improvements) | International Atomic Energy Agency | September 13, 2024 | https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/iaea-mission-to-thailand-finds-a-robust-framework-for-nuclear-security-arrangements-encourages-improvements | The same source also gives the cautionary side: the IAEA recommended improvement in a risk-informed national detection strategy, coordination among stakeholders, nuclear security culture, major-public-event planning, and training. That is relevant because 1B.3 is about whether safeguards were strengthened, not whether they were already perfect. | `1B.3` |
| [Thai Ambassador to the UN in Vienna Opened the 68th IAEA General Conference, Assumed Board of Governors Membership, and Participated in Signing Ceremony for IAEA Rays of Hope Anchor Centre to be established in Thailand](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/iaea-09162024-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | September 26, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/iaea-09162024-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand’s official 2024 IAEA statement emphasized cooperation on safe and peaceful nuclear technology and strengthening nuclear safety, security, and safeguards. This is supportive background for 1B.3, though it is not a direct statement by Srettha personally. | `1B.3` |
| [Readout of Secretary Raimondo’s Meeting with Thai Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha) | U.S. Department of Commerce | March 14, 2024 | https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/03/readout-secretary-raimondos-meeting-thai-prime-minister-srettha | Civil nuclear energy was discussed in the context of clean energy and sustainability. This is peaceful-civilian framing, not direct evidence of command-and-control discipline, but it supports the absence of escalatory or unsafe nuclear behavior. | `1B.3` |

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source showing Srettha personally ordered or tightened nuclear custody, transport, reactor safety, or emergency-response controls.
- I also did not find evidence of a nuclear incident, loss of control, or safety breakdown in Thailand during his tenure.
- So the best-supported reading is: Thailand showed a functioning and externally reviewed nuclear-security framework in 2024, with some improvements still recommended, but there is no direct ruler-specific proof of a major new safety or command-and-control initiative.
